_description: Claude-consumed JSON registry for the frontmatter pillar. Loaded by pre-write-guard.sh at runtime and read by the librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit. Carries R-32, R-33, R-37, R-39, R-40, R-64 plus the type registry, tier compliance, path-routing rules, and the universal typed cohort + property_types value-typing declarations. Frontmatter is the API every file exposes to the system; this pillar declares the fields, per-type contracts, AND the rules that enforce them. The former schemas/vault-schema.json was dissolved into this pillar (types + tier assignment + path routing) plus governance/tagging-rules.json (tag-prefix taxonomy).

cohort._description: The universal typed frontmatter cohort applied to durable in-folder notes. Scope is LOCATION-BASED: every file resident in (or symlinked into, e.g. Work/) the brain folder (vault root) is in scope; machine files parked outside the brain folder (logs, XDG state) are exempt by location, not by type. The per-type required[] lists are the real enforcement surface; universal_required (tier_compliance) is documentary. Value-typing is the write-time property_types format regex (R-64).
cohort.exempt: out-of-folder machine files (logs, XDG state); memory files (memory-auto-stamp.sh stamps created=today, so the cohort/git-date backfill would collide)

property_types._description: Value-type declarations for the universal typed cohort, consumed write-time by pre-write-guard.sh's R-64 property-typing format-regex branch (Tier 1 advisory; warn-not-DENY under the shipped default). date = ^YYYY-MM-DD; list = a YAML sequence; slug-string = ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$; int = ^[0-9]+$. Mirrored (UX-only) into a seeded .obsidian/types.json — brain-stem can seed but cannot enforce Obsidian's own property types; the enforceable layer is this format regex.

_design_notes.consumer: pre-write-guard.sh — SCHEMA_KEY case statement + R-32 type-allowlist DENY + R-33 placement advisory (reads .types[].expected_path); post-write-verify.sh — R-39 provides-presence advisory (reads .types[].canonical_scope); librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit (R-39, R-40)
absorbed_from_vault_schema: types (were top-level type keys in vault-schema.json)
_design_notes.evolution_protocol: R-37 atomic lockstep — frontmatter-rules.json + pre-write-guard.sh SCHEMA_KEY case + post-write-verify.sh type_map updated in one commit. NOTE: schemas/vault-schema.json was DISSOLVED into this pillar + governance/tagging-rules.json; the dissolved file no longer ships — author against this pillar and governance/tagging-rules.json only.

enforcement_layer: governance/frontmatter-rules.json `types` (type allowlist + per-type required/optional field declarations)
_rules.failure_mode: Files written with an unknown `type:` value or with missing Strict-tier required fields drift the schema contract silently. Downstream consumers (auto-routing, librarian, scaffold) cannot reason about the file because the contract has been violated. Without write-time DENY, the schema becomes documentation rather than enforcement — production-scale untagged-file backlogs (~500 files observed in a reference deployment) accumulate before audit catches up. The Tier 2 DENY closes the gap at the moment of capture, returning a structured error that enumerates the missing fields and points to the schema entry.
_rules.rule_text: Every Strict-tier vault write MUST declare a `type:` value drawn from the governance/frontmatter-rules.json `types` allowlist (retired types preserved in `retired_types`). For Strict-tier files, the universal required fields (`type`, `tags`, `updated`) AND the per-type `required` field list MUST all be present in the YAML frontmatter. Pre-write-guard DENIES writes failing either check; the DENY message enumerates the missing fields plus the pillar entry path. Adding a new type or extending a required-field list requires R-37 atomic lockstep updating this pillar + pre-write-guard SCHEMA_KEY case + post-write-verify type_map in one commit. Standard-tier writes emit a warning instead of DENY (operator triages via librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit); Minimal-tier writes proceed without validation.
_rules.retired_types_handling: Files declaring a retired `type:` value (currently `engagement`, `project`, `system-governance-spoke`) are DENIED with the retirement reference and per-type `replacement` guidance. For `engagement` and `project` the replacement points the author to the folder-lineage convention (field-level propagation via `engagement:` / `project:` frontmatter fields); `system-governance-spoke` retires with no replacement type (the file is now plain user content). See `retired_types` block.

enforcement_layer: pre-write-guard.sh folder-placement advisory branch (Tier 1; never blocks)
_rules.failure_mode: Files written outside the canonical folder for their declared `type:` produce structural drift that compounds — the file is invisible to type-scoped queries, lives in a folder that does not match its archetype, and creates the impression that 'this type lives anywhere.' Once the precedent lands, follow-on writes drift further. The Tier 1 advisory fires at write-time rather than waiting for weekly audit so the operator sees the misplacement at the moment of capture and can move the file before publishing wikilinks.
_rules.rule_text: Files declaring a `type:` value SHOULD reside under the canonical folder for that type per governance/frontmatter-rules.json `path_routing` (the per-archetype lineage rules). Pre-write-guard emits a Tier 1 advisory `[R-33 FOLDER PLACEMENT]` when the file's path does not match the type's expected folder pattern. The advisory never blocks — engagement-specific exceptions, cross-engagement reference docs, and adopter-customized folder structures are legitimate causes for divergence. The advisory text enumerates the expected folder pattern and the current path so the author can decide. Persistent advisory firings on the same type/folder pair surface as `placement-drift` findings in the librarian audit.

_rules._enforcement_layer_note: R-37 is documentary, not write-time-enforced. There is no `pre-write-guard.sh atomic-lockstep branch (DENY on partial-surface writes)` — PreToolUse sees one file per invocation and cannot inspect a multi-file commit set; and no `git pre-commit hook` ships with the foundation. Enforcement is git's commit-boundary atomicity (commits are atomic by construction) + author discipline at the close-out merge boundary + the librarian governance-parity-audit at audit-time.
_rules.failure_mode: Schema-touching changes that land in one surface without the others produce silent drift — the pillar declares a new type the hook does not recognize; the rule registry references a field name the pillar spells differently. Within weeks the surfaces diverge enough that no single artifact is authoritative. Drift is detectable but already-broken when the audit surfaces it. R-37's structural commitment is that partial-surface commits are treated as the error they are; the close-out merge boundary and the librarian audit are the regression checks that catch drift before it ossifies.
_rules.rule_text: The frontmatter pillar binds two coupled surfaces under R-37 atomic lockstep: (1) governance/frontmatter-rules.json (canonical pillar declaring types, tiers, path-routing rules, and rule registry; absorbed the former schemas/vault-schema.json), (2) hooks/pre-write-guard.sh SCHEMA_KEY case-statement + hooks/post-write-verify.sh type_map (runtime mirror). Adding, modifying, or retiring a `type:` value, changing a required-field list, introducing a new field class, or updating the tier-compliance contract requires touching BOTH surfaces in a single commit. R-37 is documentary — enforced via author discipline at the close-out merge boundary, git's commit-boundary atomicity, and the librarian governance-parity-audit at audit-time. There is no write-time hook branch that denies partial-surface commits (PreToolUse architecture sees one file per invocation and has no view of the multi-file commit set; the proper enforcement layer for that would be a pre-commit or post-merge audit, not pre-write-guard). This entry is the pillar-scoped instantiation of the canonical R-37 meta-rule at governance/_index.json `cross_cutting_meta_rules[]`. The coupled-surfaces declaration in governance/_index.json carries governance/foundation-master.json (forward).
coupled_surfaces: governance/foundation-master.json (forward; built from this pillar via tools/build-foundation-master.sh)

enforcement_layer: post-write-verify.sh provides-presence advisory (Tier 1; combined with R-38 blockquote-summary block)
_rules.failure_mode: Long-form files (>200 lines) without a `provides:` declaration become opaque to consumers that route by capability rather than by path. The router cannot determine what concepts the file is canonical for; the librarian cannot detect provides-canonicality drift (R-40) because there is no claim to compare against; downstream agents loading the file have no fast way to decide whether the content is relevant. The advisory surfaces the omission at write-time so the author either declares `provides:` deliberately or accepts the file as content-only.
_rules.rule_text: Files exceeding 200 lines SHOULD declare a `provides:` array in their YAML frontmatter enumerating the concepts, rules, or capabilities the file is the canonical source for. Post-write-verify emits a Tier 1 advisory `[R-39 PROVIDES PRESENCE]` when a file over the line threshold lacks `provides:` or has `provides: []`. The advisory never blocks — content-only long-form files (raw transcripts, archive imports, daily-note dumps) are legitimate and the author can ignore the advisory. The librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit tracks recurring R-39 firings as `provides-coverage-drift` findings so the operator can triage at session-close.
exemptions: Archive/** — archived content; provides-declaration is structurally unnecessary
Daily/** — daily notes are temporally-scoped, not capability-scoped
Inbox/** — aggregation surfaces; provides lives at the canonical destination, not the staging copy

enforcement_layer: drift-allowlist override at hooks/drift-allowlist.json (`provides_overlap[]` for deliberate co-canonical pairs)
_rules.failure_mode: Two or more canonical-scope files claiming the same `provides:` capability fragment authority. A consumer routing to the capability does not know which file to read; updates to one canonical do not propagate to the other; the two files drift into mutually-contradictory statements within months. Without an audit, the drift is invisible — `grep provides:` returns both files and the consumer picks one by accident. The librarian-audit finding surfaces the collision and asks the operator to either consolidate, archive one source, or register the overlap as deliberate in the drift-allowlist.
_rules.rule_text: Within the canonical-scope of the vault (vault root depth-1 + Skills/**), no two files SHOULD declare the same capability in their `provides:` array. The librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit walks every Standard- and Strict-tier file's `provides:` declaration, builds an inverted index, and emits a `provides-canonicality-drift` finding whenever a capability is claimed by 2+ canonical-scope owners. Severity is `blocking` when any owner sits at vault root; `warning` otherwise. Engagement reference docs, meeting notes, project context files, and daily notes are EXCLUDED from canonical-scope — `provides:` is project-scoped vocabulary there, not vault-wide canonical. Deliberate co-canonical pairs (e.g., a research packet plus its consumer-rendered spoke) register at hooks/drift-allowlist.json `provides_overlap[].capability` with rationale + audit-trail entry; allowlist entries mirror into librarian-manifest.json on every run and suppress the finding.
scope_exemptions: Daily/** — daily notes are temporally-scoped (foundation-shipped folder)

_exemption_classes._description: Foundation declares the EXEMPTION CLASS shape; concrete adopter folder names (engagement-scoped subfolders, project-scoped subfolders, archetype-cluster subfolders, etc.) live in overlay-master.frontmatter.canonical_scope_exemptions[]. Foundation governance stays archetype-agnostic.

classes.name: instance-scoped
classes.rationale: files inside an archetype-cluster instance (engagement / topic / repo / etc.) are scoped to that instance, not vault-wide canonical

classes.name: sub-cluster-scoped
classes.rationale: files inside an archetype's sub-cluster (project / study / epic / etc.) carry sub-cluster-scoped `provides:` vocabulary, not vault-wide canonical

enforcement_layer: pre-write-guard.sh property-type format-regex branch (Tier 1 advisory; warn-not-DENY under the shipped default)
_rules.failure_mode: Cohort fields written with a malformed value type — a free-text `created`, a scalar `tags`, a spaced `id`, a non-integer `schema_version` — are syntactically present but semantically unusable: date-range queries, list membership, slug reconciliation, and schema-version migrations all silently misfire. Obsidian Bases, an MCP server over the vault, and a RAG/GraphRAG exporter read the raw frontmatter and inherit the malformed value. Without a write-time typing signal the drift is invisible until a downstream consumer breaks. The Tier 1 advisory surfaces the type mismatch at the moment of capture so the author can correct the shape; it never blocks — the value is present, only mis-typed.
_rules.rule_text: Cohort fields declared in governance/frontmatter-rules.json `property_types` MUST carry their declared value type: `created`/`updated` a `date` (^YYYY-MM-DD), `tags` a `list` (YAML sequence), `id` a `slug-string` (^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$), `schema_version` an `int` (^[0-9]+$). Pre-write-guard emits a Tier 1 advisory `[R-64 PROPERTY TYPE]` when a present cohort value does not match its declared type; the advisory never blocks (warn is the shipped default; per-vault hard-DENY is an opt-in override). The new cohort fields (`description`/`created`/`id`/`schema_version`) join `updated` in the soft-tier non-block set — a missing cohort field warns, it does not DENY. The enforceable typing layer is this write-time format regex; the seeded `.obsidian/types.json` is a UX-only mirror (brain-stem cannot enforce Obsidian's own property types). Adding or changing a `property_types` declaration requires R-37 atomic lockstep with the pre-write-guard.sh typing branch.

tier_compliance._description: Canonical three-tier compliance definitions (absorbed from dissolved vault-schema.json `tiers` block; this pillar is now the single source of truth for tier semantics + enforcement metadata).

strict.description: System files (scaffold-emitted, /ingest-routed, scraper-aggregated to Inbox/). Hard fail at write-time (R-32 Tier 2 DENY).
strict.applies_to: type entries with tier=strict in this pillar's `types` block

standard.description: User-authored vault content. Soft warning; librarian flags drift via tag-coverage-audit + frontmatter-coverage-audit capabilities.
standard.applies_to: type entries with tier=standard in this pillar's `types` block

minimal.description: Explicit opt-out files. No validation; flagged 'outside system' by librarian. Used for legacy imports, paste-buffer scratch, archives outside lifecycle.
minimal.applies_to: files matching minimal_tier_exemptions glob patterns OR carrying explicit `tier: minimal` frontmatter directive

parent_plan.reason: Plan-tree-only field; lives in plans-schema.json + plan-manifest-schema.json, not vault content governance.
parent_plan.disposition: Deferred from v1. Re-visit when planning methodology generalizes for adopters.
parent_plan.do_not: Do NOT add `parent_plan` to any type entry in this pillar. Plan-tree files validate against plans-schema.json + plan-manifest-schema.json separately.

retired_types._description: Types removed from the active type registry; preserved for write-time DENY messaging (R-32 retired_types_handling). Absorbed from vault-schema._retired_types; replacement text abstracted off user-vocabulary folder names — concrete adopter folder patterns live in overlay-master.frontmatter.path_routing.rules[].

engagement.reason: Type information lives at file level only — folders don't have frontmatter. `engagement` is NOT a canonical TYPE; it is a FIELD slot that propagates folder lineage to files. Folders own structural artifact; field + tag propagate to file level.
engagement.replacement: Use `engagement: <slug>` as FIELD on any file living under the adopter's engagement-archetype lineage folder. Foundation declares the field; adopter's overlay-master.frontmatter.path_routing.rules[] declares the lineage glob (consultant archetype seed or extension). For the engagement-level navigation file itself, use type=`navigation`.

project.reason: Same as `engagement` — folders own project lineage; FIELD `project` propagates lineage to files.
project.replacement: Use `project: <slug>` as FIELD on any file living under the adopter's project sub-cluster lineage folder. Foundation declares the field; adopter's overlay-master.frontmatter.path_routing.rules[] declares the lineage glob. For the project-level overview file itself, use type=`context` or type=`navigation` (per file purpose).

system-governance-spoke.reason: Retired type — the foundation no longer ships in-vault narrative spokes; the governance pillar content is published in the hosted docs instead. A file declaring this type is editing a legacy spoke that is now ordinary user-owned content carrying no foundation contract.
system-governance-spoke.replacement: No replacement type. The file is now plain user content; choose an active type that fits its purpose (e.g. type=`navigation` for a folder overview, type=`reference` for a knowledge article), or leave it untracked. The governance narrative it mirrored lives in the hosted docs, not an in-vault spoke.

path_routing._description: Cross-cutting folder-lineage validation rules (absorbed from vault-schema._path_rules; renamed for clarity). Hook contract: when a file is written, evaluate matching path rules; if pattern matches, the file MUST satisfy the requires_fields + requires_tags clauses. Foundation ships an EMPTY rules[] array — archetype-specific folder patterns belong to adopter overlay-master.frontmatter.path_routing.rules[], not foundation governance. Onboarding wizard offers archetype seeds at install time and writes the adopter's selection into overlay-master. Foundation declares the SHAPE (rules[] array contract + per-rule field semantics via _rule_shape_contract below); adopter provides the CONTENT.

_rule_shape_contract._description: Per-rule object shape that adopter overlay-master.frontmatter.path_routing.rules[] entries MUST conform to. Reference contract for the wizard (onboarding successor) when authoring lineage rules into overlay-master at install time.
_rule_shape_contract.pattern: <glob path with {placeholder} segments for field-bound depth markers>
exemptions: <file-path patterns that bypass this rule (e.g., folder-level navigation/index files)>

file_type_contract_dispositions._description: Closed-world reconciliation between governance/file-type-contracts/<key>.md.json and this pillar's `types` registry. `types` is keyed by the `type:` FRONTMATTER VALUE and drives the R-32 vault-write allowlist + per-type required-field DENY, whose scope is vault-resident markdown. A file-type CONTRACT is keyed by FILE SHAPE and matched by PATH (`applies_to.path_glob`). The two key spaces are not the same set, so a contract key absent from `types` is not automatically a gap — but it must not be SILENTLY absent either. Every contract key that is not a `types` entry carries an explicit disposition here, so the reconciliation is closed-world and machine-checkable: `path-governed` (the governed file is not a vault-resident `type:`-declaring note, so a `types` entry would be inert for the real file AND would newly gate unrelated vault files declaring that value; its `governed_by` names the surface that ACTUALLY handles the file — a pillar/schema that matches it by path, or, where no pillar/schema matcher exists at all, the runtime consumer that reads the contract) or `registered-alias` (the contract governs a type that IS registered in `types` under a different key). `governed_by` must RESOLVE: the named file must ship in the foundation, and when it names a `governance/` or `schemas/` JSON it must carry a `#<dot.path>` anchor that resolves to a real entry in that file — a bare pillar name asserts governance no reader can check, which is how a row can claim a matcher that does not exist. Parity is asserted by internal/tests/ac-191-governance-matrix-parity.sh: a contract key that is neither a `types` entry nor dispositioned here FAILS, and so does a disposition row whose `governed_by` or `registered_type` does not resolve. Adding a contract file requires adding its `types` entry OR its disposition row in the same change.

_index.rationale: Not unregistered — the contract file is named for the FILE (`_index.md`) while the type it governs is `index`, which IS a `types` entry with a required-field set. The contract self-declares the mapping in its own `frontmatter_contract_source`, and governance/mandatory-files-rules.json#mandates._index_md binds the same pair.

adr.rationale: Plan-tree decision records live outside the vault-resident note surface and are governed by the plans pillar (filename_pattern + status_enum + required_sections) plus the manifest pointer array in schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json#decision_records[]. The real renderer is skills/librarian/capabilities/plan-decision-log.sh; the contract's own `_design_notes` naming plan-index is a misnomer (plan-index carries no ADR handling).

CLAUDE.rationale: The vault-root instruction file is matched by exact path and carries no `type:` frontmatter for a `types` entry to key on. NO pillar or schema matcher governs it: the only runtime handling is the vault-root write class in hooks/pre-write-guard.sh, which knows CLAUDE.md as the sole mandatory vault-root file and exempts it from the propose-and-validate prompt every OTHER new vault-root file gets. Its contract's required_sections + size_limits + prohibited_sections are documentary — none is a frontmatter required-field matter, no write-time guard consumes them, and post-write-verify.sh skips the file; the shape is carried by templates/vault-claude-md-template.md and rendered at onboard time by skills/onboarder.

doc-amender-prompt.rationale: Operator-authored prompt assets live OUTSIDE the vault in the writer state root, so the vault-scoped R-32 required-field DENY cannot reach them by construction. NO pillar or schema matcher governs them: the contract is SELF-declaring — it carries its own frontmatter_required/frontmatter_optional/frontmatter_enums — and is read directly by its runtime consumers, skills/doc-amender/process.sh and skills/govern/modes/doc-amender-prompt.sh.

episodic-chronicle.rationale: The curated episodic tier lives in the per-project memory directory, outside the vault, and its row shape is declared by the memory schema. The contract's append-only/newest-first fields are convention prose naming no write-time enforcer; its consumers are skills/librarian/capabilities/chronicle-index.sh and the session episode writer.

handoff.rationale: A plan-tree quartet member governed by the plans pillar. Its BODY shape is the enforced surface — hooks/pre-write-guard.sh reads this contract's section_schema for a write-time DENY on a malformed session heading — not a frontmatter required-field set. The renderer is skills/librarian/capabilities/plan-handoff-index.sh; the contract's own `_design_notes` naming plan-index is a misnomer (plan-index carries no handoff handling). The append-only claim in the same contract names no enforcer.

library-article.rationale: Not unregistered — the contract file is named for the ARTIFACT (a library article) while the type it governs is `reference`, which IS a `types` entry with a required-field set. The contract itself declares `type: reference`. Its size_limits are enforced audit-time by skills/librarian/capabilities/library-index.sh, which the contract states honestly.

manifest.rationale: The governed file is JSON and carries no YAML frontmatter at all, so a frontmatter `types` entry has nothing to key on. Full validation delegates to schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json (conditional-on-status). The contract's prose_prohibited rule names no enforcer in the runtime.

spec.rationale: A plan-tree quartet member governed by the plans pillar. Its contract's frontmatter_required_hints are prose-annotated HINTS (e.g. `parent_plan (depth >= 3)`), not machine-consumable field tokens, and its head_immutable_sections claim names no enforcer in the runtime. Registering the type here would retro-fire a required-field DENY across an existing plan corpus authored before any such contract.

tasks.rationale: A plan-tree quartet member governed by the plans pillar. The enforced surface is the ledger-plus-per-task BODY shape rendered by skills/librarian/capabilities/tasks-render.sh in lockstep with manifest.tasks[], not a frontmatter required-field set; the contract's own `_design_notes` naming plan-index is a misnomer (plan-index carries no tasks handling).

types._description: Canonical type registry — the foundation-shipped vault-side type entries plus retired_types reference. Each entry declares tier + per-type required + optional + conditional_required + (optional) body_structure_contract + canonical_scope (provides-presence advisory membership) + (optional) expected_path (folder-placement advisory; array of {pattern, label} per type). Adopters extend the registry via overlay-master.frontmatter.types[] (registered via `/govern register --kind file-type`) — ADD a new type, or SUPERSEDE a shipped one with a FULL replacement entry carrying `_override_reason` (R-52). A `null` overlay entry is NOT a delete and is rejected at load; there is no adopter-facing NULLIFY. Plan-tree types (spec, tasks, handoff) are governed by the plans pillar, not registered here; every file-type contract whose key is not an entry in this registry carries an explicit disposition in `file_type_contract_dispositions`.

parent_folder.condition_semantics: depth is the number of path segments between the vault root and the file; depth 1 = `<cluster>/_index.md` (parent_folder omitted because the parent IS the vault root); depth >= 2 = `<cluster>/<instance>/_index.md` or deeper (parent_folder mandatory).
parent_folder.rationale: Navigation-side lineage pointer auto-populated by post-write-verify auto-bootstrap; librarian index-maintain audits for path-vs-frontmatter drift.

generated_exemption.criterion: machine-generated, writer-owned index files: a file that is a registered writer's declared output (skills/librarian/capability-registry.json :: output_contract.writes[]) or that carries the `generated: true` frontmatter sentinel. The exempt set derives at audit time from the capability registry — the same writes[]-derived ownership the mandatory-files exemption-conflict arm uses — never a hardcoded path list.

deliverable._description: Durable, human/agent-authored work product under the Work/ surface (Work/<spoke>/deliverables/<name>.md) — the durable + human-authored context surface. Lifecycle frontmatter (status, audience) and enums are governed by governance/file-type-contracts/deliverable.md.json; the body is free-form because deliverables are heterogeneous. Enforcement fires at BOTH layers: write-time on REGISTERED-spoke Work/ writes — the pre-write-guard.sh remap prelude rewrites a registered Work/<spoke>/ write onto the vault path BEFORE the 3-tier schema block, so the write IS governed — with the librarian suite over the Work/ symlink view as the audit-time backstop for everything else (unregistered spokes, hand-authored files reached via the scoped symlink walk). A deliverable is never machine-written; the bounded exception is the sentinel-bounded generated files (the work-side directory map + the work-subfolder _index.md navigation files), a disjoint artifact class that is out of the deliverable contract. `expected_path` (Work/**) is an audit-time placement advisory, not a write-time matcher.

vault-writer._description: Per-writer reference files at Vault Writers/ describing systems writing into the vault (connectors, agentic flows, auto-research, scheduled skills, custom). Writer-kind-conditional required fields governed by governance/file-type-contracts/vault-writer.md.json.

ideation-brief._description: Plan-tree ideation brief files at ~/.claude-plans/<plan>/00-ideation-brief.md. Validated against this type registry as an interim measure; planned relocation to plans pillar type registry as a follow-up.

reference._description: Durable universal-knowledge library articles at _library/<topic>/<article>.md — one concept per file, synthesized by the librarian at promotion and scrubbed of all plan/project-specific detail. Frontmatter is the activation surface index generators read to route a reader to the article.
reference._body_shape_enforcement: A library article carries no leading in-document section index and no auto-generated table of contents (an in-doc TOC is permitted only above the soft length budget and is never auto-generated). This body-shape rule is NOT write-time-enforced — no write-time body-structure guard exists in the runtime, and the runtime ships NO synchronous write-time line-count cap at all (the former navigational hub-file max-lines guard, R-03, is RETIRED: its block was removed rather than re-pointed; declared size limits are audit-time checks). Enforcement is the library-index re-derive scan (over-threshold / shape findings, audit-time) plus the library-scrub output that synthesizes the article body. The article body-structure contract JSON is a separate file-type-contract that ships alongside the library-article template.

note._description: Thin universal raw-note type for durable hand- or machine-captured notes (work-spoke reference/ material and vault notes). Standard tier: user-authored capture is never DENY-gated — missing or partial frontmatter on a hand-written note draws at most a soft warning. The project-workspace scaffolder's --note mint stamps the full cohort plus the path_routing lineage fields (project, workstream) so machine-minted notes are conformant from birth; ephemeral scratch (daily/inbox/fleeting) stays out of scope by location.
